summary:
Each CancelSynchronousIo now runs on its own short-lived dedicated thread (`scan-cancel-attempt`), so a call the kernel holds can no longer stop the resend. The scan-cancel loop only dispatches, one attempt every 25 ms. It reserves a slot under `_gate` before `Thread.Start` and allows at most 4 live attempts. Exit, a refused Enter and Dispose first set Idle (or `_disposed`), then drain under the gate until no attempt is live. The hot path, where no cancel was issued, is still a single `Interlocked.Exchange`.

- **Premise (a):** the first build measured it before anything else was built. Each re-block was freed by the next attempt, and the held attempt then returned (6/6 interrupted, 6/6 delivered, peak 2 live, 10 of 10 runs). Premise (b) held too: the drain ended in every run, idle and loaded.
- **Acceptance command:** exits 0 in 10 of 10 runs.
- **Under 32 busy jobs:** the unfixed code was red in 10 of 10 class runs. With the fix, 30 of 30 class runs are green for both classes (`~SynchronousIoCancel`), and 30 of 30 runs of the repro class are green.
- **Answer to 'can local cancel take more than 2 s under load':** a delivered cancel does not (spike: at most 622 ms, p99 423 ms, 500 of 500, Windows 11 26200). A lost cancel does, without bound, and that was the entire flake. This answer is in the comment on `RetryMilliseconds`, and in this record.

files.why: CancelLoop now only dispatches. New StartAttempt (reserves a slot under the gate, cap 4, gives the slot back if Thread.Start throws), CancelOnce (one CancelSynchronousIo on its own thread, checks `_disposed` and CancelIssued under the gate, keeps the ObjectDisposedException catch) and EndAttempt. Leave/Drain: Idle first, then wait on a ManualResetEventSlim (spinCount 0) until no attempt is live. Used by Exit, by a refused Enter and by Dispose, which drains before it closes the handle. Adds the test-only PeakAttemptsInKernel, AttemptsLiveAtLastDrain and BeforeCancelCall seam, and comments recording the measured answer about latency over 2 s under load.
The doc comment on CancelSynchronousIo now describes the held-in-kernel behaviour as observed on Windows 11 26200. It says this contradicts the documented Remarks and names the spikes (m5).

The repro becomes the regression class, run alone in a DisableParallelization collection ResendRace. The acceptance test keeps 3 waits and the 2 s bar. A second test makes 8 waits (more than the cap) with a lost-versus-slow bar. Both check the post-Exit listing and a pending pipe wait. They report peak and live-at-Exit counts, log the time from Cancel to leaving, and restore and assert the process affinity.

Added ExitWithNoCancelMakesNoAttemptAndWaitsForNone (C-005), ExitWaitsForAttemptsAboutToCancelSoNoneLandsAfterIt (C-007 witness; red against a no-wait-drain mutant) and DisposeWithoutExitWhileCancellingEndsEveryAttemptFirst (C-008/M4). AssertNoCancelLandsOnThisThread gains an optional client delay. The flaky test CancelIsResentWhileACallBlocksAgainAfterACancel is unchanged.

m7: dropped the SL-055 copy of 'Only the cancel guard issues CancelSynchronousIo', which is SL-024's rule word for word; a comment explains why. m3: rule 2 now exempts ThreadPool.UnsafeQueueUserWorkItem (the existing Close hand-off it fired on) and adds the Task.Factory.StartNew, System.Timers.Timer and PeriodicTimer patterns.

obligations.how: C-001 is SynchronousIoCancelResendRaceTests.CancelFreesACallThatBlocksAgainBeforeTheCancelCallHasReturned: one CPU, worker at Highest, 3 waits, 2 s bar. The acceptance command exited 0 in 10 of 10 idle runs (about 100 ms from Cancel to leaving). Under 32 busy jobs it passed 30 of 30 (648 to 1565 ms, p50 955) and again inside 30 of 30 loaded class runs. Unfixed, it was red in 10 of 10 runs.

C-002: CancelIsResentWhileACallBlocksAgainAfterACancel, unchanged, run 30 times under 32 Start-Job busy loops on 16 logical CPUs (filter ~SynchronousIoCancel, blame-hang 60 s): 0 red, max test duration 1125 ms. The unfixed HEAD under the same load was red in 10 of 10 runs ('still blocked 2 s after Cancel, interrupted 1 time(s)'). Jobs were removed afterwards; 0 left.

C-003: CancelInterruptsACallBlockedInTheKernel, with its first attempt now on a newly started thread. In the 30 loaded class runs it passed every time, max 700 ms (avg 539) including the 200 ms settle. In one heavily loaded full-suite batch it failed 4 of 5 times, but only on its separate 250 ms 'Cancel() took N ms on the calling thread' bar (262 to 458 ms). Its 2 s bar never failed. That path (Thread.Start of the scan-cancel thread inside the token callback) is unchanged by this slice, and the unfixed baseline failed the same bar at 309 ms under the same load. See follow_ups.

C-004: CancelIsResentUntilACallThatHadNotReachedTheKernelIsInterrupted, unchanged. It asserts that CancelAttempts exceeds CancelsDelivered, i.e. early FALSE/1168 attempts were ignored, and that a later attempt landed. It passed idle and in all 30 loaded class runs.

C-005: new test ExitWithNoCancelMakesNoAttemptAndWaitsForNone. Guard entered on a cancellable token, never cancelled, then Exit and Dispose. It asserts Exit returns false, and CancelAttempts, PeakAttemptsInKernel and AttemptsLiveAtLastDrain are all 0, with no stray cancel on the next wait. In code, the hot path is Leave(): one Interlocked.Exchange, then return false with no lock or wait.

C-006: in both repro-class tests, attempts are still in CancelSynchronousIo when Exit is called. AttemptsLiveAtLastDrain was 2 in every idle and loaded run (asserted >= 1), and the drain always ended. Every proof loop ran with --blame-hang-timeout 60s. The one hang dump, from a loaded run, shows the test thread still in its pre-Cancel Thread.Sleep(200) with no guard activity; that was the testhost being starved, not the drain.

C-007: after Exit and before Dispose, the worker lists a TempTree folder with Directory.GetFileSystemEntries (2 entries asserted) and then waits on a pipe whose client connects 300 ms later. This is in the repro tests and in ExitWaitsForAttemptsAboutToCancelSoNoneLandsAfterIt. Both classes ran 30 times under load with this check: 0 failures.

C-008: new test DisposeWithoutExitWhileCancellingEndsEveryAttemptFirst. An exception unwinds through the using with no Exit while the canceller is still resending (at least 2 attempts after the interruption). It asserts CancelIsIssued is still true at Dispose, no stray cancel on the next pending wait, and CancelAttempts unchanged 100 ms after Dispose. It passed idle and in 30 loaded runs.

C-009: the repro class is in [Collection(nameof(ResendRace))] with [CollectionDefinition(DisableParallelization = true)], the same form as MemoryBudget and VolumeFigure. Affinity is restored in finally and asserted afterwards on a fresh Process object. Full suite with the repro included: 5 of 5 idle green, 5 of 5 green in the second loaded batch. In the first loaded batch (heavy outside load) 5 of 5 were red, but only on other load-sensitive timing tests, which the unfixed baseline also fails under the same load. The repro and the flake never failed there.

M1: the loaded loop used --filter FullyQualifiedName~SynchronousIoCancel, which matches both classes, 30 times. Per class: SynchronousIoCancelResendRaceTests 30 of 30 passed; SynchronousIoCancelTests 840 of 840 passed. The repro class was also run alone 30 more times under load: 30 of 30 passed for both tests.

M2: the post-Exit check is now a pending NamedPipe WaitForConnection, with a client after 300 ms. The mutant check confirmed the finding: a mutant whose Drain does not wait passes the repro 3 of 3, plus 5 of 5 on the first run. So I added a tests-only BeforeCancelCall seam and ExitWaitsForAttemptsAboutToCancelSoNoneLandsAfterIt, which holds attempts between the gate and the call. It goes red on that mutant 3 of 3 (and 5 of 5 earlier) with OperationCanceledException on the post-Exit wait, and is green on the real drain. The mutant was reverted; grep finds no MUTANT marker.

M3: re-blocks were run at 6 and then 8 (above the cap of 4), with the peak printed in the message and the test output. The peak does not climb per re-block: 2 in every idle run, and 3 in only 2 of 87 loaded runs. A held attempt returns once the next one interrupts the new wait, so the cap of 4 stays. The 8-wait case is a separate test in the repro class; see deviations.

M4: StartAttempt and CancelOnce refuse, under _gate, when _disposed is set or the state is not CancelIssued. Dispose sets _disposed under _gate, joins the loop, drains, disposes the event, and only then closes the SafeThreadHandle. DisposeWithoutExitWhileCancellingEndsEveryAttemptFirst asserts CancelAttempts does not grow after Dispose.

m1: the dispatcher reserves the slot (_live++, event reset) under _gate before Thread.Start. A catch around Start gives the slot back. CancelOnce gives it back in finally on every path, including when it finds the state not CancelIssued. So the cap and the drain both count every live attempt, and nothing leaks.

m3: rule 2 now reads \bThreadPool\.(?!UnsafeQueueUserWorkItem\b), plus Task.Run, Task.Factory.StartNew, QueueUserWorkItem, new Timer(, System.Timers.Timer and PeriodicTimer. Checked with .NET regex against SynchronousIoCancel.cs: 0 hits (the old \bThreadPool\b hit 1, line 215). No comment in the file names these APIs, and the settled rule matches code only. RuleCases C-001, ArchitectureRulesTests and RuleCopiesAgreeTests are green.

m4: every proof loop ran dotnet test with --blame-hang-timeout 60s --blame-hang-dump-type mini, through a temp script (%TEMP%/sl055-proof/loop.ps1). One hang was dumped and analysed with dotnet-dump, installed to a temp tool path and since removed. The accepted risk is recorded in the Drain comment and here: a production Exit or Dispose drain has no watchdog, and an attempt held after the worker left all I/O would hang the scan thread. Never observed in more than 200 runs, on Windows 11 26200 only.

m5: the Kernel32.CancelSynchronousIo remarks and the class remarks both call the held-in-kernel behaviour 'observed on Windows 11 26200'. They quote the documented Remarks it contradicts, and name SL-055's risk spikes and the regression test.

m6: idle and loaded full-suite runs, reported separately. Idle: 5 of 5 green (301 tests). Loaded batch 1 (heavy outside load, 111 to 131 s per run): 5 of 5 red, only on CancelInterruptsACallBlockedInTheKernel's 250 ms Cancel() bar, CancellationTests.CancelReturnsFromAScanStuckInItsFirstCall's 250 ms Cancel() bar and CancelAtRandomMomentsEndsEveryScanCleanlyAndLeavesNoStrayCancel ('0 completed'). Loaded batch 2: 5 of 5 green. Unfixed baseline under load: heavy runs 2 of 2 red (the flake, CancelAtRandomMoments, the Cancel() bar, ScanStoreRollupTimingTests); lighter runs 2 of 3 red, on the flake only.

m7: I diffed .taad/fitness.yaml. The engine had appended both SL-055 rules once, at lines 606 to 626. I appended nothing; I removed the duplicate of SL-024's rule (with a YAML comment saying why) and corrected rule 2. RuleCases C-001 held under powershell.exe and pwsh ('AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns; 34 settled entries'). ArchitectureRulesTests and RuleCopiesAgreeTests passed.
Owed to validate-slice; evidence from this build: the exact command exited 0 in 10 of 10 idle runs on the final build. It now runs 2 tests (3 waits and 8 waits), both passing.

Owed to validate-slice; evidence: with one CPU and the worker at Highest, 6 of 6 and then 8 of 8 re-blocks were interrupted, with every attempt delivered (TRUE) and a peak of 2 live. So a second CancelSynchronousIo from another thread reaches the new wait while the first is still held.

Owed to validate-slice; evidence: held attempts returned, with CancelsDelivered equal to attempts, and Exit's drain ended in every run: about 20 idle, 90 loaded repro runs and 30 loaded class runs, all with blame-hang 60 s. No drain hang was dumped.

Owed to validate-slice; evidence: ExitWaitsForAttemptsAboutToCancelSoNoneLandsAfterIt is red against a no-wait-drain mutant (OperationCanceledException on the post-Exit wait, 8 of 8) and green on the real code. CancelAttempts does not change after Exit in the repro tests.

deviations: M3's 'repro re-blocks at least 6 times' is a second test in the same serialized class: CancelFreesACallThatBlocksAgainMoreTimesThanTheCapOfLiveAttempts, 8 waits, with a 10 s lost-versus-slow bar. The acceptance repro keeps 3 waits and the 2 s bar. Measured: the 6-wait repro pinned to one CPU under 32 busy jobs took 1.1 to 2.05 s from Cancel to leaving, and failed the 2 s bar in 1 of 28 runs with all 6 waits interrupted. That is starvation of the single pinned CPU, not a lost cancel, and it would have made the validate loops noisy, which this slice exists to stop. The 3-wait repro under the same load: 648 to 1565 ms over 30 runs.

M2's check cannot be proved by the repro alone. Against a mutant whose Drain does not wait, the post-Exit pending wait in the repro stays green (8 of 8), because on one CPU no attempt is between the gate and its call when Exit runs. I added a tests-only seam, BeforeCancelCall (the same idiom as BeforeCall and AfterCall), and ExitWaitsForAttemptsAboutToCancelSoNoneLandsAfterIt. That test goes red on the mutant (8 of 8) and is the witness for the drain.

A refused Enter also drains, through the shared Leave(). The design named only Exit and Dispose, but Enter's refused path set Idle directly. An attempt admitted in that window could still have been in flight after Enter returned false.

Attempts and reservations require state == CancelIssued, not 'not Idle'. The code has three states (Idle, InCall, CancelIssued), and a refused Enter briefly sets InCall. Admitting attempts on InCall would let one run past a Leave whose previous state was InCall, which does not drain.

For the gate and drain (taste fork left to the build), I kept the existing System.Threading.Lock _gate and waited on a ManualResetEventSlim with spinCount 0. Lock has no Wait or Pulse, and a spinning waiter at Highest priority on one CPU would delay the attempts it waits for.

Architecture rules (m7, m3): the design's rule 1 was dropped from fitness.yaml because it is SL-024's rule to the letter. Rule 2 now exempts ThreadPool.UnsafeQueueUserWorkItem (the existing Close hand-off) and gains three patterns.
Two test-only counters added: PeakAttemptsInKernel (M3) and AttemptsLiveAtLastDrain, which is how the tests show Exit was called with attempts still live (C-006).

'Restore thread priority in a finally block' is not built as code. The Highest priority belongs to the test's own dedicated thread, which ends with the test. Only ProcessorAffinity is process-wide; it is restored in finally and asserted afterwards.
not_built: No file under .taad/slices/SL-055 was written by hand; index.json is derived by the engine. The answer about cancels over 2 s under load is in the code comments and in this build record, which the engine stores as build-slice-1.json. Delivered cancels: at most 622 ms (spike, 500 of 500). Lost cancels: unbounded. After the fix, the one-CPU repro under 32 busy jobs leaves in 648 to 1565 ms.

No cap-behaviour test that holds 4 real kernel calls (C-010, non-material by design). The finally-block release was covered by review, and the 8-wait test shows the cap is never reached (peak 2, and 3 in 2 of 87 loaded runs).
follow_ups: Other load-sensitive timing bars fail under full suite plus 32 busy jobs, in both the unfixed baseline and the fix: the 250 ms 'Cancel() took N ms' bar in SynchronousIoCancelTests.CancelInterruptsACallBlockedInTheKernel and in CancellationTests.CancelReturnsFromAScanStuckInItsFirstCall (Thread.Start of the scan-cancel thread inside the token callback); CancelAtRandomMomentsEndsEveryScanCleanlyAndLeavesNoStrayCancel's calibration ('0 completed, 100 cancelled'); and ScanStoreRollupTimingTests' 250 ms budget. This answers the design's open question: under load, CancelInterruptsACallBlockedInTheKernel fails on the prompt-Cancel bar (262 to 458 ms), not the lost-cancel mechanism. A separate slice.

The one-CPU acceptance repro under 32 busy jobs ran 648 to 1565 ms against its 2 s bar (30 of 30 green), so the tail margin is about 22%. If validate's loaded loops see it cross, the test's own single-CPU starvation is the likely cause (all waits interrupted). Pinning to the highest CPU instead of CPU 0 (which takes most interrupts) is a candidate.

Production Exit and Dispose drain without a watchdog, which is the accepted risk of the unbounded drain (O-006, m4). The held-attempt behaviour was measured only on Windows 11 26200. Windows 10 is unmeasured.

Loaded loops met machine-wide starvation twice: a 2-minute test discovery with a blame-hang dump taken while the test thread was still in its pre-Cancel Sleep(200), and one 'Failed to negotiate protocol ... 90 seconds'. Validate's loaded protocol may want VSTEST_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT raised and should treat runs with no test result as infrastructure failures.
Rule 2's exemption lets ThreadPool.UnsafeQueueUserWorkItem appear anywhere in SynchronousIoCancel.cs, not only in Close. Fitness has no per-method scope, so review has to catch misuse.
